questions.prompt: What do Pip and Stone find when they reach the loud noise?
choices: A very small toadling with its mouth wide open.
A huge troll shaking the marsh trees.
A family of foxes splashing in the water.
questions.answer: A very small toadling with its mouth wide open.
questions.evidenceText:
On a mossy stone in the marsh sat a toadling.
It was very small.
Its mouth was very wide open.
All the noise was coming from it.

questions.prompt: Why has the little toadling been making such a loud sound?
choices: It is lost and calling for its family.
It is warning everyone away from the marsh.
It is practising for a singing contest.
questions.answer: It is lost and calling for its family.
questions.evidenceText:
"I am lost," it said.
"I was calling for my family."

questions.prompt: What lesson does Stone's response to the frightened toadling show?
choices: Someone can be large and gentle at the same time.
Stone thinks becoming smaller is the best way to help.
Stone thinks Pip should lead because Pip looks less scary.
questions.answer: Someone can be large and gentle at the same time.
questions.rationale: Stone says he is large but gentle, then uses his own very loud voice to call for the toadling's family; this shows someone can be large and gentle at the same time.
questions.evidenceText:
"You are very large," said the toadling.
"Yes," said Stone.
"But I am gentle."

supportingEvidence.evidenceText:
Stone stood up and called out across the marsh.
It was the loudest sound Pip had ever heard.
Louder than the toadling.
Much louder.
Something answered from the far side of the marsh.
